# Connectix API

> Connectix is a Bulgarian messaging platform for online shops: SMS, Viber and Noti messages from approved templates, fallback flows (Viber first, SMS if undelivered), one-time passwords, a shared phone blacklist, TrustCheck (cash-on-delivery risk rating of a shopper) and courier shipment tracking with webhooks.

Version 1.2.0. Base URL for every example: `https://api-sandbox.connectix.bg` (the sandbox: delivery is simulated and nothing is billed). Authenticate with the `Authorization` header: the sandbox token as-is, or `Bearer <token>`. Send `Accept: application/json`. Phone numbers are E.164 (`+359...`).

## Guides

- [Quickstart](https://mcp.connectix.bg/docs/quickstart.md)

## Endpoints

### Templates

Approved message templates of the company; every message is sent from one.

- `GET /templates` — `listTemplates`: List message templates

### Messages

Send SMS, Viber and Noti messages, fallback flows and Viber documents.

- `POST /messages` — `sendMessage`: Send a message from a template
- `GET /messages` — `listMessages`: List messages
- `GET /messages/{id}` — `getMessage`: Get a message
- `POST /messages/fallback` — `sendFallbackMessage`: Send a message with fallback steps
- `POST /messages/media` — `sendMediaMessage`: Send a document over Viber

### OTP

One-time passwords over SMS: send, verify, resend.

- `POST /otp/send` — `sendOtp`: Send a one-time password
- `POST /otp/verify` — `verifyOtp`: Verify a one-time password
- `POST /otp/resend` — `resendOtp`: Re-issue a one-time password

### Integrations

Integrations group the traffic of one external system and own the webhook hooks.

- `POST /integration/register` — `registerIntegration`: Register an integration
- `POST /integration/unregister` — `unregisterIntegration`: Remove an integration
- `POST /integration/register/hook` — `registerIntegrationHook`: Register a webhook hook on an integration
- `POST /integration/unregister/hook` — `unregisterIntegrationHook`: Remove a webhook hook

### Blacklist

Phones that must not be messaged; shared with the console and the stop/resume word automation.

- `POST /blacklist` — `addToBlacklist`: Check whether a phone is blacklisted (deprecated alias) (deprecated, sunset 2027-03-31)
- `POST /blacklist/check` — `checkBlacklist`: Check whether a phone is blacklisted
- `POST /blacklist/toggle` — `toggleBlacklist`: Add, update or remove a phone in the blacklist

### TrustCheck

Cash-on-delivery risk rating of a shopper, computed from tracked shipments.

- `POST /shopper/check` — `checkShopper`: Check the TrustCheck risk rating of a shopper

### Tracking

Register courier shipments so Connectix tracks them and posts tracking webhooks.

- `POST /shipments` — `createShipment`: Register a shipment for tracking

### Account

Information about the authenticated application and reference data.

- `GET /me` — `getMe`: Identify the application behind the token

## Webhooks

- `callback` — Posted each time the delivery status changes: to the message's own `callbackUrl` when it has one, otherwise to every active `callback` hook of the integration the message was sent with. Messages sent from campaigns never trigger it. Delivered as an HTTP `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json` and `User-Agent: connectix-client`, from the public address range of Connectix. Every event carries `eventId` in the body and as the `X-Connectix-Event-Id` header. **Signature.** Deliveries to an integration hook are signed with the integration `secret` (the one you chose at `registerIntegration`): `X-Connectix-Timestamp` is the Unix time of the delivery and `X-Connectix-Signature` is `v1=` followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `"<timestamp>.<raw request body>"` keyed with the secret. Verify with a constant-time comparison and reject timestamps older than 5 minutes. Deliveries to a per-message `callbackUrl`/`inboundUrl` have no secret and are not signed - validate the `id` against your own records instead. **Acknowledging and retries.** Answer any 2xx within the timeout (5 s, 10 s for tracking events) and do the work afterwards. A non-2xx answer (429 included) or a timeout is retried per URL with growing delays: 30 s, 1 min, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30 min, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 hours - 12 more attempts over about 32 hours, after which the event is dropped for that URL (the hook stays active). Redirects are not followed. Delivery is at-least-once and the order of events is not guaranteed: deduplicate on `eventId` (or on `id` + `status` for the `callback` event) and order by the event's own timestamp.
- `inbound` — Posted when the recipient replies: to the message's own `inboundUrl` when it has one, otherwise to every active `inbound` hook of the integration the message was sent with. Replies equal to the application's stop/resume word also toggle the blacklist automatically. Delivered as an HTTP `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json` and `User-Agent: connectix-client`, from the public address range of Connectix. Every event carries `eventId` in the body and as the `X-Connectix-Event-Id` header. **Signature.** Deliveries to an integration hook are signed with the integration `secret` (the one you chose at `registerIntegration`): `X-Connectix-Timestamp` is the Unix time of the delivery and `X-Connectix-Signature` is `v1=` followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `"<timestamp>.<raw request body>"` keyed with the secret. Verify with a constant-time comparison and reject timestamps older than 5 minutes. Deliveries to a per-message `callbackUrl`/`inboundUrl` have no secret and are not signed - validate the `id` against your own records instead. **Acknowledging and retries.** Answer any 2xx within the timeout (5 s, 10 s for tracking events) and do the work afterwards. A non-2xx answer (429 included) or a timeout is retried per URL with growing delays: 30 s, 1 min, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30 min, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 hours - 12 more attempts over about 32 hours, after which the event is dropped for that URL (the hook stays active). Redirects are not followed. Delivery is at-least-once and the order of events is not guaranteed: deduplicate on `eventId` (or on `id` + `status` for the `callback` event) and order by the event's own timestamp.
- `blacklist` — Posted to the `blacklist` hooks of the application (or of every application of the company when the entry is `global`) whenever an entry is created or changed. Delivered as an HTTP `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json` and `User-Agent: connectix-client`, from the public address range of Connectix. Every event carries `eventId` in the body and as the `X-Connectix-Event-Id` header. **Signature.** Deliveries to an integration hook are signed with the integration `secret` (the one you chose at `registerIntegration`): `X-Connectix-Timestamp` is the Unix time of the delivery and `X-Connectix-Signature` is `v1=` followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `"<timestamp>.<raw request body>"` keyed with the secret. Verify with a constant-time comparison and reject timestamps older than 5 minutes. Deliveries to a per-message `callbackUrl`/`inboundUrl` have no secret and are not signed - validate the `id` against your own records instead. **Acknowledging and retries.** Answer any 2xx within the timeout (5 s, 10 s for tracking events) and do the work afterwards. A non-2xx answer (429 included) or a timeout is retried per URL with growing delays: 30 s, 1 min, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30 min, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 hours - 12 more attempts over about 32 hours, after which the event is dropped for that URL (the hook stays active). Redirects are not followed. Delivery is at-least-once and the order of events is not guaranteed: deduplicate on `eventId` (or on `id` + `status` for the `callback` event) and order by the event's own timestamp.
- `template` — Posted to the `template` hooks of every active integration of the company within a minute after a template is created or changed, so the integration can keep its local template list in sync with `listTemplates`. Delivered as an HTTP `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json` and `User-Agent: connectix-client`, from the public address range of Connectix. Every event carries `eventId` in the body and as the `X-Connectix-Event-Id` header. **Signature.** Deliveries to an integration hook are signed with the integration `secret` (the one you chose at `registerIntegration`): `X-Connectix-Timestamp` is the Unix time of the delivery and `X-Connectix-Signature` is `v1=` followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `"<timestamp>.<raw request body>"` keyed with the secret. Verify with a constant-time comparison and reject timestamps older than 5 minutes. Deliveries to a per-message `callbackUrl`/`inboundUrl` have no secret and are not signed - validate the `id` against your own records instead. **Acknowledging and retries.** Answer any 2xx within the timeout (5 s, 10 s for tracking events) and do the work afterwards. A non-2xx answer (429 included) or a timeout is retried per URL with growing delays: 30 s, 1 min, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30 min, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 hours - 12 more attempts over about 32 hours, after which the event is dropped for that URL (the hook stays active). Redirects are not followed. Delivery is at-least-once and the order of events is not guaranteed: deduplicate on `eventId` (or on `id` + `status` for the `callback` event) and order by the event's own timestamp.
- `tracking` — Posted to the `tracking` hooks of the application that registered the shipment (`createShipment`) when the courier reports a new state. Delivered as an HTTP `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json` and `User-Agent: connectix-client`, from the public address range of Connectix. Every event carries `eventId` in the body and as the `X-Connectix-Event-Id` header. **Signature.** Deliveries to an integration hook are signed with the integration `secret` (the one you chose at `registerIntegration`): `X-Connectix-Timestamp` is the Unix time of the delivery and `X-Connectix-Signature` is `v1=` followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of `"<timestamp>.<raw request body>"` keyed with the secret. Verify with a constant-time comparison and reject timestamps older than 5 minutes. Deliveries to a per-message `callbackUrl`/`inboundUrl` have no secret and are not signed - validate the `id` against your own records instead. **Acknowledging and retries.** Answer any 2xx within the timeout (5 s, 10 s for tracking events) and do the work afterwards. A non-2xx answer (429 included) or a timeout is retried per URL with growing delays: 30 s, 1 min, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30 min, 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 hours - 12 more attempts over about 32 hours, after which the event is dropped for that URL (the hook stays active). Redirects are not followed. Delivery is at-least-once and the order of events is not guaranteed: deduplicate on `eventId` (or on `id` + `status` for the `callback` event) and order by the event's own timestamp.
